verdicts.reason: Reproduced with the URL parser browsers use: new URL("/\\evil.example/x", "https://antaeus.app/settings/").href is https://evil.example/x, and "/<tab>/evil.example/" resolves to https://evil.example/ as well; URLSearchParams decodes %5C and %09 into those characters, so /settings/?returnTo=/%5Cevil.example/ reaches safeReturnTo as a string that starts with one slash and passes both checks (continuity.ts:87-92). The value becomes the href of the back link (back-button.tsx:51, navigation.tsx:83). continuity.test.ts:59-70 covers absolute, '//' and scheme forms only. The proposed function closes the hole, but it resolves against window.location.origin: under the unit-test DOM (happy-dom, vitest.config.ts:23) the page is about:blank, whose origin is the string "null", and new URL(path, "null") throws, so every path, including "/quota-workback/", would return null and the existing 'accepts in-domain paths' test would fail. A fixed base gives the same answer in every environment.
verdicts.finalProposed: const RETURN_BASE = "https://antaeus.invalid"; export function safeReturnTo(returnTo: string | null): string | null { if (!returnTo || !returnTo.startsWith("/") || returnTo.startsWith("//")) return null; if (/[\\\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(returnTo)) return null; try { const u = new URL(returnTo, RETURN_BASE); if (u.origin !== RETURN_BASE) return null; return u.pathname + u.search + u.hash; } catch { return null; } } Add to continuity.test.ts: safeReturnTo("/\\evil.example/") and safeReturnTo("/\t/evil.example/") are null; safeReturnTo("/quota-workback/?a=1#x") is returned unchanged; the existing cases still pass.

The main defect is real. Nothing under src/pilot-desk/v4 calls setOutcome (grep: only ds/components/ForgeForm.tsx:140 and components/ForgePanel.tsx:212 do), so a pilot saved on the default screen keeps outcome 'not_started' (types.ts:104), stored as outcome_state 'open' (poc-bridge.ts:67-72). The scheduled check selects every 'open' row and, once created_at + duration_days has passed, writes '… passed its readout window N days ago with no recorded outcome' (generators.ts:270-312); the day count changes daily, so the notice is rewritten each day and returns after a dismissal, and the default screen has nowhere to record the outcome. The round-trip effect is also real ('not_started' -> 'open' -> 'in_progress', poc-bridge.ts:81-89). One side claim does not hold: the finding says results never reach Founding GTM or Readiness because the outcome never becomes converted or failed. Neither reads that value: Readiness counts any saved pilot whose stored outcome is not the literal 'open' (readiness-aggregator.ts:217-239, so 'not_started' counts), and no Founding GTM section tests the pilot outcome. On the fix: adding a control to step 5 changes a screen whose design the owner settled (CLAUDE.md Part I §4.15), so the control itself, not only its wording, needs the owner's approval.
verdicts.finalProposed: OWNER DECISION, with this as the recommended change: on step 5 of the default screen, next to 'Copy results summary', add one labelled choice 'How did the pilot end?' with 'Still running' (in_progress), 'The buyer moved forward' (converted) and 'The buyer did not move forward' (failed); choosing one calls setOutcome and then saveProof(saveDraft()), so outcome_state becomes passed or failed and the scheduled check stops for that pilot. Set outcome to in_progress when step 1 is saved. No decision needed for the rest: in poc-bridge.ts write data.outcome beside outcome_state and prefer it in rowToProof, so 'Not started' survives a cloud round trip. Tests: a state test (choosing 'The buyer moved forward' saves outcome converted) and a poc-bridge test (not_started survives proofToInsert -> rowToProof). The date the check counts from (row creation, not the pilot's recorded start) stays an owner decision as stated.

verdicts.reason: bootCloudPersistence inserts a new pipeline_settings row when none carries the quota marker (cloud-persistence.ts:78-95) and saveInputsToCloud inserts whenever no row id is held (119-124). The one-row-per-user constraint is not in this repository's SQL, but three places attest to it: src/lib/data-migration.ts:380-383 ('Schema enforces 1 pipeline_settings row per user'), the 2026-04-24 session log in CLAUDE.md ('pipeline_settings had UNIQUE(user_id) so insert collided with founder's existing row'), and the earlier app's write, which upserts on user_id (js/supabase-config.js:2398-2400; an upsert on that column only works with a unique constraint). For a user who already has an unmarked row, the insert is rejected, boot returns 'local-only', and each later save repeats the failed insert. Medium confidence is the right rating because the live schema cannot be read from here; the fix is safe whether or not the constraint is present. One gap in it: only the boot step merges. Later saves go through inputsToUpdate, which replaces the whole data column (quota-bridge.ts:108-117), so the earlier payload the fix set out to keep (data.migrated_from_localstorage) would be dropped on the second save.
verdicts.finalProposed: Reuse the user's existing row and merge on every write. In quota-bridge.ts add inputsToMergedUpdate(existingData, inputs) returning { data: { ...existingData, kind: KIND_QUOTA_INPUTS, inputs } }.
